notes: Perfect match on C66, C67. Both agree that APP fails to induce AChR clustering in LRP4/MuSK knockout myotubes, demonstrating APP requires both proteins to function.

Perfect match on C79, C80, C135. Both agree all three agrin isoforms bind APP. Peer reviewers use this finding to challenge functional interpretations elsewhere but do not dispute the binding data itself.

Perfect match on C81, C82. LLM finds prepatterning is maintained in double mutants (supported observation). Peer reviewers want additional experiments to determine if APP/APLP2 are required for prepatterning, rating this UNCERTAIN.

Perfect match on C89, C90, C100, C101, C102. Both rate as UNCERTAIN the hypothesis that APP-LRP4 interaction can promote initial AChR clustering independent of agrin. Both note the idea is interesting but requires additional experimental validation.

High overlap on C53, C54, C55 (60% Jaccard). LLM finds genetic interaction data with quantitative morphological analysis sufficient. Peer reviewers find the fluorescent images show only subtle impairment and request quantitative analysis, suggesting existing quantification may be insufficient.
High overlap on C71, C72, C73, C74 (57% Jaccard). Both accept the dose-dependent biphasic effects of agrin on LRP4-APP interaction as supported by biochemical data.

High overlap on C33, C59, C60, C62, C63, C114 (55% Jaccard). LLM finds APP can independently activate MuSK and induce AChR clustering. Peer reviewers state this is UNSUPPORTED because C2C12 cells express muscle agrin, confounding the interpretation of agrin-independence.
Moderate overlap on C38, C39, C40 (50% Jaccard). Both accept the phenotypic characterization of Lrp4ECD/ECD mice showing the extracellular domain is sufficient for initial NMJ formation.

Moderate overlap on C31, C57, C58 (43% Jaccard). LLM finds APP-LRP4 binding well-supported by biochemical assays. Peer reviewers acknowledge binding is 'strong and convincing' but rate UNCERTAIN because they find no direct evidence that APP anchors LRP4 ECD at the NMJ (C85, C86 in peer result).

Moderate overlap on C46, C47, C49 (43% Jaccard). LLM finds Lrp4ECD/ECD mice demonstrate membrane anchoring is required for postnatal maturation. Peer reviewers call this a 'misinterpretation' (UNSUPPORTED) because many maturation events were normal, including synapse elimination and subunit switching.
Moderate overlap on C31, C32 (40% Jaccard). Both agree the biochemical demonstration of APP-LRP4 interaction is strong and convincing.

Moderate overlap on C83, C84 (40% Jaccard). LLM finds LRP4 concentration at NMJs and APP co-localization supported with quantified statistics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting developmental expression profiles showing spatial and temporal correlation.

Low overlap on C85, C86 (29% Jaccard). LLM R11 addresses localization data showing diffuse LRP4 in mutants. Peer R1 questions whether APP anchors LRP4 ECD at NMJ, requesting additional localization experiments. Partial overlap in claims but both concern LRP4 localization mechanism.

Low overlap on C41, C42 (25% Jaccard). Both accept that Lrp4ΔICD/ΔICD mice develop normal NMJs, demonstrating the intracellular domain is dispensable. LLM R7 includes additional claims about synapse size; peer R14 groups with other phenotypic observations.

Low overlap on C57 only (20% Jaccard). LLM finds APP-LRP4 binding supported. Peer reviewers note no data shows the LBD domain is required for full-length LRP4 interaction with APP, rating domain-specific requirement as UNCERTAIN.
Low overlap on C68 only (20% Jaccard). Both accept co-immunoprecipitation data showing APP, LRP4, and MuSK form a stable complex in muscle. Peer reviewers do not challenge this biochemical evidence.

Low overlap on C70 only (14% Jaccard). LLM accepts agrin's biphasic effect and RAP-Fc control. Peer reviewers question whether RAP-Fc binds LRP4 (no data presented) and are uncertain about the dimerization conclusion.

Low overlap on C48 only (13% Jaccard). LLM groups C48 with other claims about Lrp4ΔICD mice having normal NMJs. Peer R7 focuses on the interpretation that membrane anchoring is required for postnatal maturation, which they find UNSUPPORTED.

Low overlap on C89 only (9% Jaccard). Both question agrin-independent APP function but with different emphasis. LLM rates hypothesis as UNCERTAIN (plausible but needs validation). Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED due to muscle agrin confound in C2C12 cells.
